lessons.title: Using Context to Choose Words
lessons.concept: Cloze tests present a passage with blanks and require selecting words that fit grammatically and contextually. Read the surrounding sentences to understand tone, meaning, and logical flow before choosing an option.
lessons.formula: Approach: read full sentence/passage context -> determine required meaning/part of speech -> test options in the blank.
lessons.worked_example: Sentence: 'Despite the heavy rain, the match continued _____ schedule.' The context implies no delay, so 'on schedule' fits; 'behind schedule' would contradict 'continued despite the heavy rain'.
mistakes: Choosing a word that fits locally but not the overall meaning
Not reading beyond the immediate sentence when context spans multiple sentences

lessons.title: Grammar and Collocation in Blanks
lessons.concept: Correct cloze answers must satisfy grammar (tense, subject-verb agreement, articles, prepositions) and natural word combinations (collocations). Even if meaning seems close, an option may be wrong if it breaks grammar or common usage.
lessons.formula: Check: tense/time markers, agreement, preposition/article use, and common collocations (e.g., 'make a decision', not 'do a decision').
lessons.worked_example: Sentence: 'She is interested _____ learning new skills.' Correct preposition is 'in': 'interested in learning'.
mistakes: Focusing only on meaning and missing grammatical fit
Using incorrect prepositions with common adjectives/verbs
Selecting words that form unnatural collocations

lessons.title: Logical Flow and Connectors
lessons.concept: Blanks may require connectors (however, therefore, although) or words that maintain logical flow (cause-effect, contrast, addition). Identify the relationship between clauses/sentences to choose the appropriate connector or transition word.
lessons.formula: Contrast -> however/although/but; cause-effect -> therefore/because/so; addition -> moreover/and/also.
lessons.worked_example: Sentence: 'He studied hard; _____, he scored well.' The second clause is a result, so 'therefore' fits: 'He studied hard; therefore, he scored well.'
mistakes: Using contrast connectors for cause-effect relationships (or vice versa)
Ignoring punctuation clues (semicolon/comma) that signal connector usage
Choosing a connector that reverses the intended logic

practice.question: Choose the correct word: 'She was tired, _____ she completed the work on time.'
practice.explanation: The sentence shows contrast: being tired vs completing work on time. 'But' correctly expresses this contrast.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Choose the correct word: 'He is good _____ mathematics.'
practice.explanation: The correct preposition/collocation is 'good at' when referring to skill or ability in a subject/activity: 'good at mathematics'.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Choose the correct word: 'It rained heavily; _____, the streets were flooded.'
practice.explanation: Flooded streets are a result of heavy rain. 'Therefore' indicates cause and effect and fits after a semicolon in this structure.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Choose the correct word: 'The manager asked everyone to _____ attention to the new guidelines.'
practice.explanation: The correct collocation is 'pay attention' (to give notice or focus). 'Give', 'put', and 'make' do not form the standard phrase here.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Choose the correct word: 'Although he was new to the team, he adapted _____.'
practice.explanation: The verb 'adapted' is modified by an adverb describing how he adapted. 'Quickly' is the correct adverb form.
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'The instructions were clear, _____ everyone understood what to do.'
questions.explanation: Clear instructions led to understanding; this is a cause-effect/result relationship. 'So' correctly connects the clauses.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'She has been working here _____ 2019.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time (2019) to indicate when an action started and continues. 'For' is used with a duration.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'He did not study for the test; _____, he failed.'
questions.explanation: Failing is the result/consequence of not studying. 'Consequently' expresses this cause-effect relationship appropriately.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'Please _____ a look at this document before the meeting.'
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'take a look', meaning to examine or view something briefly.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'The new policy aims to improve efficiency _____ reducing unnecessary delays.'
questions.explanation: 'By' + gerund ('by reducing') is used to indicate the method or means through which the aim is achieved.
questions.provenance: Authored original question; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.
